judgments.reasoning_cat1: The granting language is standard, though 'approximately 10.89 acres' and the transcription slips ('parcel!', 'any and ail', 'made apart hereof') leave minor slack about what is conveyed and rely wholly on Exhibit A. The catch-all 'all rights, privileges, easements and appurtenances, if any, thereunto belonging' is a general phrase riding on enumerated specifics, but its reach is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grant of interests in the beds of adjoining streets sits alongside Sections 3 and 5, which contemplate that Sixth and Abbott Streets will be vacated and new legal descriptions created, so what Exhibit A describes may not match what is finally conveyed. Section 1's assignment to Buyer of awards for change of grade also sits uneasily with Section 12, which gives condemnation awards to Seller on termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause twice refers to 'deductions identified below' and 'setoffs as described below' when no deductions or setoffs are in fact described anywhere, and it mixes an illustrative TIF example with the operative payment formula, leaving the timing and source of the $1,000,000 Outstanding Balance genuinely uncertain. The interest sentence ('to the same extent, if any, that either or both the City... pay interest... on the outstanding incurred eligible expenses') is opaque on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 28 repeats the last sentence but says 'less any setoff' where Section 2 says 'less any deductions', and Section 8(a)(i) says the whole 'Purchase Price, plus or minus prorations' is to be paid to Seller at Closing, which contradicts the deferred $1,000,000 mechanism here. No other provision supplies the missing schedule of deductions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deed must convey title 'free from any and all liens or encumbrances' yet 'subject only to' Permitted Exceptions defined by reference to an Option Agreement whose date is left blank, so the defining document is not identified. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4 speaks of 'those Permitted Exceptions attached hereto' and the attachment list includes 'Exhibit B — Permitted Exceptions', while this section defines Permitted Exceptions by reference to the Option Agreement instead; the two sources may not coincide. judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cure mechanic is garbled: Seller 'shall have ten (10) business days prior to the date of Closing' to cure is not a workable period, and Buyer must elect 'prior to the expiration of the period for Seller to remedy' — a period that is itself undefined. Blank spaces ('the office in ____') and 'expanse' for 'expense' add mechanical defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to 'Permitted Exceptions attached hereto' conflicts with Section 3, which defines them by reference to the unattached Option Agreement. judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation has no deadline and is conditioned only on execution, while its content depends on 'the City of Detroit's final approved plat of vacation and dedication of right of way' that may not exist; 'as a prepared in accordance with' is a mechanical slip. Whether Seller must procure the City's approval or merely reflect it if given is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs in parallel with Section 3's deed obligation, which depends on the same municipal approval, and with Section 8(a)'s ninety-day closing deadline, creating a possible impossibility if the City has not acted. Nothing elsewhere allocates responsibility for obtaining the vacation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The as-is acceptance is broad and qualified only in its middle sentence by 'except as expressly set forth elsewhere in the Agreement', leaving unclear whether the first and third sentences are similarly qualified. 'All faults of every kind and nature whatsoever whether latent or patent and whether now or hereafter existing' is sweeping and one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against Section 7(d) and 7(e) environmental representations and against Section 11, under which Seller bears risk of loss and must repair injury 'beyond the ordinary wear and tear' before deed delivery. Harmonising an unqualified acceptance of the closing-date condition with Seller's repair duty is a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory lead-in; the only wrinkle is that it labels the following items both 'covenants' and 'represents', which can matter for remedy. Standing alone there is little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the closing warranty paragraph that follows and with Section 23's no-merger/survival rule. No conflicting provision identified.
